name: HOMER
what_it_is: HOMER is a carrier-grade, scalable packet and event observability framework for VoIP/RTC monitoring that captures and correlates SIP, RTP, and RTCP traffic using the HEP/EEP encapsulation protocol. It provides instant search, call flow analysis, and QoS metrics through a web dashboard backed by standard observability storage APIs.
configuration: Storage backend selection (PostgreSQL, Loki, Elasticsearch, qryn)
modes: Headless observability (API-only, no built-in UI storage)
constraints: Does not include a built-in SQL database — requires external storage backend (PostgreSQL, Loki, Elasticsearch, or qryn)
Capture requires a separate agent (heplify or captagent) — the server does not perform passive packet capture on its own
Licensed under AGPL-3.0, which imposes copyleft obligations on network-service deployments
No native Windows support — designed for Linux hosts
notable_absences: No built-in storage engine — depends entirely on external databases
No native visualization engine — relies on Grafana or compatible dashboards
docker-compose.yml not present in the main sipcapture/homer repository (lives in sipcapture/homer-docker)
